features.name: lvnDetection.ts + LVN/HVN eval harness (Phase B)
features.description: Phase B of the LVN/HVN detection effort. lib/engine/lvnDetection.ts: pure, immutable detector over an HTF VbP volume series ({price,volume}[]; no paired delta needed) that returns HVN (high-volume-node peaks) and BOTH LVN types — HVN peaks also feed feat-015 magnetCheck. LVN detection is DUAL-MECHANISM: (a) VALLEY LVNs = local minima between two distributions (prominence/depth detection); (b) TAPER-EDGE LVNs = the shoulder/knee where a distribution tapers into a flat, sustained low-volume plateau (gradient/derivative or relative-threshold-crossing-into-plateau) — a pure local-minima pass MISSES these (e.g. fixture-1 labels 30008/30088 are taper edges, not valleys). Physically meaningful params (neighborhood window, valley/peak prominence/depth threshold, plateau flatness + level for the taper detector); may optionally re-bin a fine (e.g. 1-tick) input series. LVN/HVN output is authoritative and code-owned (no vision round-trip). scripts/lvn-eval.ts (+ npm run lvn:eval): loads each Phase-A fixture + its LVN/HVN labels, greedily matches detected<->labeled levels of the same type by nearest within an ABSOLUTE price tolerance (configurable, default +/-10 points — these are trading levels that align with MGI, NOT bin-relative), computes precision/recall + count delta per type per fixture, prints a per-fixture + aggregate table, reports train vs holdout separately, exits nonzero only when the TRAIN set is below threshold. Colocated unit tests exercise detector mechanics on synthetic series (single valley/peak, flat profile, double distribution, noisy shoulders, AND a taper-edge case: distribution -> low plateau).
features.evidence: lib/engine/lvnDetection.ts: pure, immutable detectLvnHvn(series:{price,volume}[], overrides?) over an HTF VbP volume series (no paired delta). Returns HVN peaks (topographic prominence) + BOTH LVN types — VALLEY (prominence/depth of a trough between distributions) and TAPER-EDGE (relative-threshold-crossing-into-a-flat-low-plateau, gated on a real distribution shoulder just outside the knee) — so a pure local-minima pass no longer misses taper shoulders. Thresholds are RELATIVE (fractions of peak/POC volume) so one param set generalizes across fixtures with 10x-different raw magnitudes; a moving-average smooth de-noises the 1-point bins; output is descending-price to match the export convention. Plain TS types, no Zod, no file I/O (mirrors sibling engine modules). scripts/lvn-eval.ts + `npm run lvn:eval`: loads each Phase-A fixture (loadLvnFixtures, strict) and greedily matches detected<->labeled levels of the same type by nearest within an ABSOLUTE ±10pt tolerance (configurable via --tolerance), computes precision/recall + count-delta per type per fixture, reports TRAIN and HOLDOUT aggregates separately, and exits nonzero only when TRAIN F1 (LVN or HVN) < 0.40 (--threshold, a REGRESSION FLOOR not a quality claim). Detection is code-owned and authoritative — the LLM is NOT asked to confirm/adjust node prices (feat-018) — so accuracy is what ships. FIXTURE RE-LABEL: the feat-033 labels had been padded toward a ~9-per-type target, putting many LVN labels on high-volume bins (e.g. fixture-1's 30200 was in BOTH lists and is the POC); all 8 relabeled to genuine structure (HVN peaks; LVN troughs/taper-knees), then snapped to nearest real extrema. Tuned result (Config B, chosen for generalization over train-max to avoid holdout overfit): TRAIN LVN F1 0.46 / HVN F1 0.69 (gate PASS); HOLDOUT LVN 0.36 / HVN 0.61 (reported, never tuned against). HVN detection is solid; LVN localization is the known-hard part (architecture's #1 engine risk) and this is an honest first cut — improving it is future work (better taper algorithm / more fixtures). lib/engine/lvnDetection.test.ts: 10 synthetic mechanics tests (single-peak hill, double-distribution valley, flat profile, <3-bin guard, shoulder-noise robustness, taper-edge knee, no-plateau negative, descending-order + peakVolume, no-mutate, tuned-defaults). ./init.sh green: typecheck 0, lint 0 errors (3 pre-existing warnings), 196 tests pass (19 files, +10), next build OK.

features.name: terrainZones.ts
features.description: Contiguous Stratosphere->Abyss zone stack with the No-Gap invariant (Price[N]===Price2[N+1]); classify regions by volume (acceptance/HVN vs rejection/LVN) cross-referenced with delta sign (absorption vs initiative). Engine assembles + validates borders. MGI-ANCHORED BORDER PROMOTION (doctrine: knowledge/doctrine/chart-reading.md 'Internal partitioning' + 'Valley+MGI=Trench, Shelf+MGI=Wall, Peak+MGI=Magnet'): a raw acceptance border (LVN valley/shelf) only becomes a HARD PARTITION when a major MGI level (from feat-012 mgiPriority) aligns with it. Anchor the classification on the MGI levels: for each major MGI, inspect the LOCAL volume profile and classify it — deep valley between two blocks -> Trench (Iron Trench); high-volume block dropping off sharply into a void with the MGI at the shelf edge -> Wall (Iron Ledge; overrides the bell-curve read — wVWAP at a block edge is a Wall, not a Magnet); MGI surrounded by thick roughly-equal volume with no distinct dip -> Magnet (invalidation — cannot be a structural border or a T3 Campaign Max). THIS IS THE HOME FOR HARD-LEDGE DETECTION: the standalone feat-014/035 LVN detector deliberately does NOT chase tall/shallow ledges (a whole-profile ledge scan is unseparable from ordinary distribution flanks by a threshold — investigated + rejected in feat-035, net-negative). Anchoring on the few MGI prices instead avoids that false-positive explosion, so the local shelf/valley test here should FAVOR RECALL: the MGI cross-reference can only PRUNE a spurious border, never CREATE a missing one, and detection is code-owned (feat-018: the LLM cannot add/adjust node prices), so a missed shelf-at-MGI is unrecoverable while an extra flagged shelf is cheap (dropped unless it happens to sit on an MGI). Consumes lvnDetection LVN/HVN output (feat-014) + Summary POC/VAH/VAL (feat-002) + MGI levels (feat-012). NOTE: the Magnet-side check overlaps feat-015 magnetCheck (POC/VAH/VAL/HVN vs MGI); keep the Magnet-Check logic single-sourced between the two (share a helper or have terrainZones consume magnetCheck's magnet classification rather than re-deriving it).
features.evidence: lib/engine/terrainZones.ts: pure, immutable engine module. assembleTerrain({profile,lvn,summary,mgi,params?}) does two jobs. (1) MGI-ANCHORED BORDER PROMOTION: selectAnchorLevels(mgi) picks major anchors (Tier-1 + Rip, deduped, price-desc); classifyBorder inspects the LOCAL VbP shape around each anchor (center band ±centerHalfPts vs left/right flank maxima within flankWindowPts, normalized to the local peak) and promotes with strict doctrine priority Trench > Wall > Magnet > mgi — Trench=center dip flanked by blocks both sides (Valley+MGI); Wall=block one side dropping into a void with MGI at the edge, checked BEFORE Magnet so a block-edge MGI is a Wall not a Magnet (Shelf+MGI, the HOME FOR HARD-LEDGE DETECTION); Magnet=thick both sides/no dip AND aligned with a POC/VAH/VAL/HVN (invalidation, cannot be border/T3); else plain mgi. Recall-favoring per spec (MGI cross-ref can only PRUNE, never CREATE; missed shelf-at-MGI unrecoverable downstream). Magnet set + alignment SINGLE-SOURCED from feat-015 magnetCheck (collectMagnets/classifyMagnet); detector LVN/HVN nodes (feat-014) attached as corroboration. (2) ZONE ASSEMBLY: hard partitions (Trench/Wall) + profile extremes divide the range into a contiguous Stratosphere->Abyss stack with the No-Gap invariant (zone[N].bottom===zone[N+1].top) held by construction and validated by validateContiguity; each zone classified by volume (acceptance vs void, mean>=acceptanceFrac*peak) x delta sign (buying/selling/balanced -> absorption/initiative/neutral) and given a vertical-map position relative to currentPrice (killbox=price zone, stratosphere/abyss=extremes, attic=above, foundation/elevator-shaft=below by void-ness). BorderKind matches Briefing schema LevelKind. No MGI-terrain eval fixtures exist so thresholds are documented recall-favoring doctrine heuristics in DEFAULT_TERRAIN_PARAMS, overridable. Doctrine basis: chart-reading.md 'Internal partitioning' (Valley+MGI=Trench, Shelf+MGI=Wall, Peak+MGI=Magnet) + 'Vertical campaign map'. lib/engine/terrainZones.test.ts: 20 tests (anchor selection Tier1+Rip/dedup/order; Trench/Wall/Magnet/plain-mgi/outside-range classification; magnet single-source gating; hard-partition filter; detector corroboration; No-Gap contiguity + full-range span + split-at-partition; acceptance/void; killbox/stratosphere/attic/foundation/abyss/elevator-shaft positions; delta initiative-vs-absorption + unknown-when-no-delta; <2-bin degenerate; currentPrice passthrough). ./init.sh green: typecheck 0, lint 0 errors (3 pre-existing warnings), 234 tests pass (21 files, +20), next build OK.

features.name: riskReward.ts
features.description: Direction-aware 3:1 R/R gate; enforce 'stops never widen' vs the prior briefing. Produces rr for each Objective.
features.evidence: lib/engine/riskReward.ts: pure, immutable engine module. evaluateRiskReward({direction,entry,stop,targets,rrMin?,priorStop?}) computes direction-aware risk (long: entry-stop; short: stop-entry) and per-target reward/rr, headline rr to the nearest target (T1), gates rr>=rrMin (DEFAULT_RR_MIN=3.0 mirroring seeded config.rr_min), and enforces 'stops never widen' vs the prior briefing (long: new stop lower than priorStop = farther = invalid; short: higher; 0.25-tick EPSILON tolerance). Returns RiskReward{risk, targets[], rr, rrMin, meetsGate, priorStop, stopWidened, valid, reasons[]} with human-readable invalidation reasons (wrong-side stop/target, below-minimum, widened). objectiveRiskReward(objective, {rrMin?,priorStop?}) adapts a schema Objective via type-only import (no runtime Zod coupling): entry=Entry A, stop=farthest protective-side stop (most conservative R/R), targets in listed order; throws when no entry or no protective-side stop. features.evidence: REALTIME/RLS DECISION: Broadcast, not postgres_changes. All tables are RLS-locked with no policies (service-role only); postgres_changes would need anon SELECT policies on briefings+eval_results, exposing FULL rows (briefing content, model output) to any anon-key holder via the REST Data API. Instead migration supabase/migrations/20260708120000_realtime_notifications.sql (committed, NOT applied live -- no DB credentials in this container) installs an AFTER INSERT trigger on both tables that calls realtime.send() with a MINIMAL payload {type,id,status,created_at} on the private topic 'gekko:alerts', plus a realtime.messages SELECT policy for anon/authenticated scoped to extension='broadcast' AND that single topic. No table data exposed, no supabase_realtime publication change, one channel for both tables; trigger fn has an exception guard so a Realtime hiccup can never fail the INSERT. CLIENT: first browser Supabase client lib/supabase/browser.ts (anon key, cached, returns null without env -- never imported server-side); app/components/alerts-center.tsx ('use client', mounted in app/layout.tsx so the subscription survives navigation) does explicit opt-in (Enable Alerts button requests Notification permission -- no auto-prompt), then channel(GEKKO_ALERTS_TOPIC,{config:{private:true}}) + realtime.setAuth() + on('broadcast',{event:'insert'}) firing page-context Notifications ('New briefing ready' / 'Entry eval: <STATUS>' via lib/notifications/events.ts buildAlertContent shared with the push path), with connection status shown (Live/Connecting/Realtime error/No Supabase env/Blocked in browser). features.name: Staleness detection
features.description: At button-press time (briefing or eval), check bundle freshness: if the latest bundle is older than a margin, surface a staleness warning and mark the result stale; UI marks briefings/eval results stale; never serve stale as fresh.
features.evidence: lib/engine/staleness.ts: pure, serializable assessStaleness({receivedAt, now?, marginMs?}) → StalenessAssessment {isStale, hasData, ageMs, ageSeconds, marginMs, receivedAt, evaluatedAt, warning}. Compares the latest raw_bundles.received_at against a freshness margin (DEFAULT_STALENESS_MARGIN_MS = 180s, ~6 missed 30s exports; overridable); >margin ⇒ stale, and null/unparseable receivedAt (no uploader/Sierra) ⇒ maximally stale (hasData=false, ageMs=Infinity). Boundary is strictly-greater (==margin is fresh); future-dated bundles clamp to age 0 (clock skew). Stale results carry a human warning ('do not treat as the live market picture') for the UI; fresh ⇒ warning=null — never serve stale as fresh. Engine primitive for the not-yet-built consumers (analyze-task feat-018, eval-task feat-025, render pages feat-019/025), mirroring ripStatus/riskReward. LANGSMITH TELEMETRY: lib/observability/telemetry.ts lazily builds ONE private NodeTracerProvider per worker process (BatchSpanProcessor -> RedactingSpanExporter -> OTLPTraceExporter proto) pointed at LangSmith's OTLP ingestion (https://api.smith.langchain.com/otel/v1/traces, headers x-api-key: $LANGSMITH_API_KEY + optional Langsmith-Project: $LANGSMITH_PROJECT; LANGSMITH_OTEL_ENDPOINT override for EU) and hands its tracer to the AI SDK via experimental_telemetry.tracer. generateStructured gained an OPT-IN telemetry param (recordInputs+recordOutputs on, functionId groups traces); analyze passes {functionId:'analyze-task'}, eval {functionId:'eval-task'}. ENV-GATED: without LANGSMITH_API_KEY getLlmTelemetry() is null and experimental_telemetry is omitted entirely (offline tests unaffected); flush is awaited per call but failures are swallowed so a LangSmith outage can never fail a run. features.description: Raise LVN (Low Volume Node) localization quality in lib/engine/lvnDetection.ts. CONTEXT: after feat-014's fixture re-label + Config-B tuning, HVN detection is solid (~0.61-0.69 F1 at +/-10pt) but LVN is weak — TRAIN LVN F1 0.46 / HOLDOUT 0.36 — the architecture's acknowledged #1 engine risk. CANDIDATE DIRECTIONS (seeds only — the user has ideas to fold in, and additions to the fixture set are in scope): improve the taper-edge algorithm (the plateau/shoulder heuristic misses trend-elongated tails); per-shape or adaptive params instead of one global set; better valley localization (sub-bin / centroid of the trough rather than the min bin); re-binning the 1-tick series; expand the fixture set beyond 8 (thin train signal); revisit the +/-10pt tolerance as a product decision. features.evidence: feat-035 (2026-07-06): Caleb re-labeled all 8 fixtures to his real methodology — HVNs = only the most prominent (1 on clean/trend, 3-4 on multimodal); LVNs = SHELF EDGES / the start of a low-volume area between distributions / where volume drops off a cliff, NOT troughs (confirmed per-label: fixture-8 30470 is the top of a ledge, fixture-7 29980/30270 are volume shelves, fixture-6 29250 is the start of a low area). This moved the ground truth and broke the old gate (train LVN F1 0.33). TWO algorithm changes in lib/engine/lvnDetection.ts: (1) HVN dominance floor `hvnDominanceFrac` (0.35) — an HVN must be prominent AND tall, cutting over-detection (train HVN det 27->15 vs 12 labeled, precision 0.41->0.73); (2) shelf-edge generalization — `plateauLevelFrac` 0.18->0.30 (catch moderate-volume shelves) and the distribution shoulder is sought within `shoulderWindow` (40pt) rather than only the adjacent bin. Re-tuned TRAIN-only via a throwaway grid sweep (58k configs, not committed); picked a stable moderate config (sw17 pp0.2 hd0.35 vd0.1 pl0.3 pr6 sf0.6 shw40 mt14) favoring generalization over train-max. RESULT (npm run lvn:eval, +/-10pt): TRAIN LVN F1 0.51 / HVN 0.81 (was 0.33/0.56 against the new labels) — gate PASSES at 0.40; HOLDOUT LVN 0.36 / HVN 0.43 (honest, never tuned). KNOWN REMAINING LIMITATION: shallow tall ledges that sit high on a distribution (e.g. fixture-7 30270 @54% peak, on a ~50%-of-peak flat) are still missed. Investigated a relative-contrast / high-side gradient-knee ledge detector (4 variants, incl. moving the target ledge into train) — it catches a tall ledge only at a step threshold that also fires on the ordinary flanks of every distribution, so it is a NET NEGATIVE on train (catching one ledge costs ~8 false LVNs; train F1 48->43). Root cause: a big ledge and a normal distribution flank are not separable in the 1-D volume-by-price shape by a threshold; distinguishing them needs a width/shape-aware model or the chart image (forbidden — code-owned detection). Kept the precise baseline. Caleb re-reviewed fixture-8 on the chart and dropped its 30470 label (mid-distribution, not a ledge), keeping the 30347/30541 boundary lows. NO re-binning (Caleb confirmed the CSV bins ARE the 4/8-tick chart bars — no resolution mismatch). Tests: lib/engine/lvnDetection.test.ts 13 pass (added HVN-floor + windowed-shoulder cases). init.sh green.

features.name: Effort-vs-result absorption prints (level-free order-flow reversal signal)
features.description: Bundle-data math review (2026-08-07, session following the Codex delta-intensity redundancy claim): prototype validation on two live bundles (2026-08-06 18:33 UTC, 630 bars; 16:26 UTC, 534 bars) found one order-flow construct with a real, replicated edge that the engine does not compute. An effort-vs-result absorption print is an exec bar where aggression was heavy but price refused to move: |delta| >= the 75th percentile of the series' |ask-bid| AND candle body <= 25% of the bar's high-low range. When such a bar prints after a directional move (>10 pts net over the prior 10 bars), price reversed within the next 10 bars 64%/71% of the time vs a 57% base rate, and the mean 10-bar move AGAINST the prior trend roughly doubled (+13.2/+15.9 pts vs +7.1/+7.9 baseline) — consistent across both bundles. This is Wyckoff effort-without-result made numeric, and it fills a real gap: stallConfirmation is level-anchored (needs a candidate border), while this detector is level-FREE — it fires anywhere on the tape, including at levels the briefing never mapped. Implementation: extend computeBarFlow (lib/engine/barFlow.ts) with an absorptionPrints reduction — count in the recent window, plus the most recent print's side (absorbing buys vs sells, from delta sign vs prior-move direction), price, and bars-ago — computed from existing ExecBar fields only (no new export columns); thresholds (P75 delta percentile, 25% body fraction, 10-pt/10-bar prior-move qualifier) as named exported constants for the doctrine drift guard. Surface via engineFacts into the analyze/update and eval prompts as raw facts (advisory context, not a gate), alongside the existing climax/divergence lines. Keep the detector distinct from DeltaIntensity semantics: it uses raw bid/ask columns only.

Measured on the 2026-08-06 bundle: median bar duration 45s, p10 16s, p90 369s — a 23x dynamic range in how fast the market is trading. Pace is a CONTEXT feature, not a directional trigger (after 4x-pace bursts: 18 continuations vs 11 reversals — no standalone edge), so it must ship as descriptive telemetry, never a gate. Value: (1) pace climax into a border is the numeric form of the doctrine's exhaustion cone / climactic-participation read; (2) dead tape (p90+ durations) marks absent participation — moves on dead tape are suspect; (3) the eval near-entry gate's proximity_window_seconds (default 60s) currently holds anywhere from 1 to 4+ bars depending on pace, silently changing what 'recent' means — surfacing current pace lets the eval prompt (and operators tuning the window) see that. features.name: Price impact per unit of order flow (Kyle's lambda)
features.description: Bundle review 2026-08-07 B3 (docs/data-bundle-review-2026-08-07.md): regress per-bar (close-open) on per-bar delta over a rolling window. Lambda is the quantitative statement of absorption -- low lambda means aggressive flow is being met without price moving, high lambda means the book is thin and small flow travels far. Measured on bundle 1c15934a: whole-session lambda 83.7 pts per 1000 net delta (R^2 0.27); rolling 30-bar min 18.2 / median 76.4 / max 155.0, a 9x spread, with the lowest-lambda windows (08:23, 09:20, 08:03) reading as absorption and the highest (06:29, 01:13, 09:57) as vacuum. Honest caveat to carry into the implementation: per-window R^2 runs 0.02-0.44, so lambda is a noisy estimate and the fact MUST carry a confidence gate -- report only when R^2 and window volume clear a threshold, else null, following the degradation pattern the other engine facts already use. The signal is the CHANGE in lambda, not its level. Generalises the current absorption scan, which can only see stacks that happen to fall inside the ~25-bin delta profiles; lambda works everywhere price has traded. Relationship to feat-089: that feature's effort-vs-result absorption PRINT is the same idea as a binary per-bar test (heavy |delta|, small body); lambda is its continuous, windowed form. Ship feat-087 first -- it has replicated base-rate-controlled evidence and this does not -- then use lambda for the regime read the print cannot give. PRIOR NEGATIVE RESULT (2026-08-07 delta-intensity review, branch claude/delta-intensity-redundancy-xe1bbj): lambda was tested AS A TIMING FILTER and rejected -- 60 percent vs a 58 percent base rate, i.e. near-nil. That does not refute this feature, which scopes lambda as a continuous liquidity/absorption REGIME read feeding the narrative and gating other signals, not as a trigger; but it does mean lambda must clear its own base-rate control in that framing before it ships, and it sits below feat-087 and feat-094 in priority until it does.

features.name: HTF order flow — cumulative delta and swing-level divergence
features.description: Bundle review 2026-08-07 B5/D4 (docs/data-bundle-review-2026-08-07.md): parseHtfBars produces volume, bidVolume, askVolume and a computed delta per bar; grepping the three consumers (htfStructure, multiDayTpo, overnightSession) finds zero references to any of them -- 87 days x 2916 bars of 30-min order flow parsed, typed, documented and feeding nothing. htfStructure locates swing highs and lows from OHLC and stops there, while the delta at those swings sits in the same rows. Add multi-day cumulative delta, delta and volume at each confirmed swing, and divergence between a fresh HTF price extreme and HTF cumulative delta. These are the exact analogues of what barFlow already computes on the execution timeframe -- the code pattern exists and needs pointing at the other bar series. PRIOR NEGATIVE RESULT (2026-08-07 delta-intensity review): DAY-LEVEL HTF delta divergence was tested as a fade signal and rejected (slight continuation bias). Scope this feature accordingly -- swing-level annotation and cumulative-delta context for the narrative, not a day-level fade trigger -- and control against the unconditional base rate before surfacing any directional claim. The same review independently confirmed the parsed-but-unused finding (parseHtfBars computes delta; nothing downstream reads it), without filing a feature for it.
features.evidence: 2026-08-12 (branch feat-102-htf-order-flow): shipped as lib/engine/htfFlow.ts -> EngineFacts.htfFlow, wired into analyze, update and eval. SCOPE CUT BY MEASUREMENT: a base-rate control study ran in parallel on 3,559 union'd HTF bars pulled from three live Supabase bundles (2026-04-26..2026-08-12, 78 trading days, 6x the repo fixture) and found swing-level delta divergence has NO empirical support -- 89 divergent swings, the fade thesis UNDERPERFORMING the unconditional base rate by 6.7/5.6/6.7/11.3 pp at h=4/8/16/34 bars, every 95% CI containing the base rate, nothing surviving Holm, and 1 of 64 grid cells at raw p<0.05 against 3.2 expected by chance. It replicates the 2026-08-07 day-level rejection at swing level; the only replicable direction is CONTINUATION, i.e. opposite to what the label implies. Operator decision: divergence is COMPUTED and unit-tested but WITHHELD from every prompt payload, pinned by gates in tests/prompt-data-sync.test.ts and tests/eval.runEval.test.ts -- re-enabling is a one-line change at a marked seam in lib/analyze/prompt.ts and lib/eval/prompt.ts. Second study finding, also enforced in code: cumulative delta ran OPPOSITE to realised price direction on 60 of 78 trading days (77%), and its level is anchor-dependent by construction, so there is NO bare signed total -- every net delta names its anchor bar and ships paired with the price change over that same window, per RTH session too. What ships as the feature's real deliverable is per-swing delta/volume annotation on the same confirmed swings htfStructure reports (swings print ~55% more volume than a typical bar; swing-high delta skews mildly positive, swing-low negative). Power note: divergent swings arrive at 1.14/trading day, so a 5 pp lift would need ~700 trading days -- the 90-day rolling export can never answer this. Full study + reproduction: docs/htf-delta-divergence-study-2026-08-12.md, scripts/studies/htf-delta-divergence/. Verification: ./init.sh EXIT=0 -- typecheck clean, lint clean, 1395 passed | 1 skipped (76 files), next build compiled.

features.name: Empirical reversal statistics per level class
features.description: Bundle review 2026-08-07 B8 (docs/data-bundle-review-2026-08-07.md): feat-086's contract asks the model for the nearest level with 'a decent probability of reversal', and no probability is computed anywhere. The 61 RTH sessions in every bundle's HTF export can measure it. First touch of prior-session levels on a 3h horizon, reversal excursion vs continuation excursion: PDH n=29 edge 1.13, PDL n=20 edge 1.31, PDC n=34 edge 1.76, prior-day mid n=28 edge 1.51, against an any-bar baseline of 1.16. Two warnings that must survive into the implementation. (1) n of 20-34 per class is far too small to trade off -- this establishes that the METHOD is feasible on data already present, not that PDC carries a 1.76 edge; the statistic needs months of accumulation, ideally persisted across bundles rather than recomputed from one 90-day window. (2) The first cut of this measurement scored 'P(reversal >= 50 pts)' at 100 percent for every level class -- and for the unconditional baseline too, because 50 pts is 0.18 sigma (see feat-096). Every statistic here MUST be reported against its unconditional baseline or it is theatre. Done properly, over the level classes the engine actually uses (AAA vs A borders, LVN valleys, one-sided vs balanced HVN builds), this turns the doctrine's qualitative level ranking into a measured one.

features.name: Double-distribution detection within the session profile
features.description: Bundle review 2026-08-07 C3 (docs/data-bundle-review-2026-08-07.md): a bimodal session profile with a low-volume gap between two distributions is a distinct regime the engine has no name for. multiDayTpo finds interior LVN valleys ACROSS sessions, but nothing looks for the shape WITHIN the day. Apply the standard treatment -- a dip test or a two-component mixture fit over the session volume profile (feat-098) or the TPO ladder -- and surface the two distribution centres, the separating valley and a confidence, so the briefing can name a double-distribution day and treat the valley as the structure it is rather than as an ordinary LVN.

features.name: Scheduled-event calendar as an engine fact
features.description: Bundle review 2026-08-07 A3 (docs/data-bundle-review-2026-08-07.md): the system has no notion of time-to-event. A briefing generated at 07:55 CT ahead of an 08:30 CPI print and one generated on a quiet Tuesday are treated identically, and the doctrine has nothing to say about standing down into a release. It also explains volume anomalies that feat-094's RVOL will otherwise surface as unexplained participation swings.

features.name: Data export: timezone and session metadata on every export
features.description: Bundle review 2026-08-07 A5 (docs/data-bundle-review-2026-08-07.md): every export writes naive local timestamps and the engine hard-codes the 08:30 CT RTH open (RTH_OPEN_MINUTES in overnightSession.ts, consumed by sessionIntraday, multiDayTpo and the daily-session reconstruction). features.name: ATR-projected price levels as anchorable structure
features.description: Operator direction 2026-08-09, following the feat-089..097 batch review: the operator uses ATR as a PRICE LEVEL for targets and reversals -- 'current price plus one ATR' is a target, 'swing low minus one ATR' is where a reversal is expected -- not as a normalizer. The engine today exposes ATR only in the normalizer role: htfStructure.atrPoints as a raw scalar, rotation.extentAtr, and currentVsSwings.fromLastSwingHighAtr / fromLastSwingLowAtr (all feat-049), plus an eval-prompt line framing 'a few ATR' as rotation noise. No ATR-derived PRICE exists anywhere in the engine, so engineAnchorPrices() cannot host an entry, stop or target on one and the model can only produce ATR-projected prices as freehand arithmetic in prose -- exactly the off-anchor advisory that feat-090 and feat-097 eliminated for the value and VWAP levels. Work: project ATR from a small, defensible set of reference prices into concrete price rungs and feed them into engineAnchorPrices() through the same optional-argument seam feat-090 established for value levels (do NOT touch engineZoneBorders -- an ATR projection is not a zone partition, per the boundary feat-097 set). Reference anchors should cover the two uses the operator named: projections from current price (target rungs both directions) and from the last confirmed swing high and swing low (reversal rungs), at named exported multiples (start with 0.5/1.0/1.5/2.0x and justify the set against the measured distribution rather than shipping round numbers unargued). Each rung must carry its reference and multiple as an attribution label a briefing can quote, in the style of feat-097's vwapRungs. Note the scale relationship before choosing multiples: one 30-min ATR is ~110 pts, which is ~0.4 sigma and therefore almost exactly feat-096's significant-move floor -- so a 1x ATR projection sits at the minimum reversal room the engine already demands, and multiples below 1x will mostly fail that gate. Say so in the fact rather than emitting rungs that silently cannot host an objective. Must degrade to null/empty when htfStructure is null (no HTF export) or atrPoints is 0, and must not fabricate a swing-anchored rung when no confirmed swing exists. Surface via engineFacts into the analyze/update prompts as anchorable structure. This feature does NOT change the existing ATR-normalized distance fields -- it adds the price-level role alongside them.
features.evidence: lib/engine/atrProjection.ts (+ colocated atrProjection.test.ts, 9 tests): projects the 30-min ATR into anchorable PRICES at ATR_PROJECTION_MULTIPLES = 0.5/1/1.5/2x -- from current price both directions (target rungs) and OUTWARD from the last confirmed swing high/low (reversal rungs). Each rung carries reference, referencePrice, signed multiple, projectionPts, a quotable attribution label ('current price (29945.75) +1x ATR') in feat-097 vwapRungs style, and clearsSignificantMove. Measured on the chart-data fixture: ATR 116.23 pts, session sigma 295.12 pts, significant-move floor 0.4 sigma = 118.05 pts -- so 1x ATR = 0.394 sigma lands 1.82 pts UNDER the floor. 16 rungs: current price 30178.21/30120.10/30061.98/30003.87 and 29887.64/29829.52/29771.41/29713.29; swing high 28032.75 -> 28090.87/28148.98/28207.10/28265.21; swing low 27603.50 -> 27545.38/27487.27/27429.15/27371.04. 8 of 16 (every 0.5x and 1x rung) are flagged clearsSignificantMove:false and the fact SAYS SO in significantMoveNote rather than emitting them silently; the flag resolves per run against scaledGates (under the unmeasured-sigma 50-pt fallback the same 0.5x rungs clear -- a static filter would have been wrong). Regression pinned in tests/analyze.engineFacts.test.ts (5 tests): every rung is IN engineAnchorPrices() at distance 0, additions are purely additive, the zone stack is 10 zones / 11 borders before AND after, and both the fact and its anchor contribution degrade to null/no-op with no HTF export. features.name: MGI hierarchy: VRange 1x-zone merge, Rip partition, nearest-daily distance
features.description: Operator review of the MGI importance hierarchy 2026-08-10, three findings. (1) VRange is IMPLIED-VOLATILITY geography, not traded structure, and the +-2/+-3 extensions are the two edges of ONE shaded zone. Per the Sierra Implied Vol Ranges study's definition (supplied by the operator mid-session, correcting an earlier reading that fitted them to range-width multiples), every level is the session OPEN +- a multiple of D, the expected session move implied by VIX: high/low at 0.25xD (the study's Upper/Lower Ranges, value-area-like mean reversion, NOT range extremes), and the ext* levels at 0.90xD and 1.00xD -- the NEAR and FAR edges of the shaded 1x Range Zone. features.name: Recency-weighted session sigma + significant-move floor 0.4σ → 0.3σ
features.description: The 2026-08-11 briefing (bundle b6f71b2e, price 29654) put its primary short entry 246 pts above the market and its secondary long 203.5 pts below it, on a day whose prior session had a 181.25-pt TOTAL range. The model was compliant: the promoted terrain borders were 29900 / 29718.75 / 29631.75 / 29450.5 — spans of 181.25, 87 and 181.25 pts — price sat inside the 87-pt span, and the significant-move floor resolved to 145.56 pts, so the only entry→T2 pairs clearing the floor were the outer two and the entry-first contract's 'walk outward to the FIRST qualifying level' rule had nowhere nearer to stop. Two independent causes, both fixed here. (1) THE ESTIMATOR. feat-095 aggregated per-session Parkinson variance as a flat RMS over 10 sessions. That is the textbook estimator for a STATIONARY process and this one is not: squaring let a single 898-pt session carry ~27x the weight of a 181-pt one, and a flat window cannot see a regime turn, so the module reported 363.9 pts while the last three sessions ranged 445/296/181 and the engine's OWN dailyRanges fact read 'contracting'. Backtested over the 60 RTH sessions in that bundle's export (each candidate predicting the NEXT session's realized sigma, 40 test points), the flat RMS was the WORST of seventeen candidates swept: RMSE 153.4, +58.6 pt mean bias, 65% of sessions landing under its forecast. Replaced with a recency-weighted mean of per-session SIGMA (ewMeanSigma, decay 0.75, ~2.4-session half-life): RMSE 133.9, bias +27.6. Weighting the VARIANCE was tried first and rejected — it only moved the live estimate 364 → 271 even at lambda=0.70, because squaring dominates any weighting. The 10-session median scored best on RMSE (127.4) and was nearly unbiased, but it is a flat window wearing a robust hat — it read 352.8 on the same export, i.e. it does not turn either. The window stays at SIGMA_ESTIMATION_SESSIONS=10: 1-0.75^10 = 94.4% of the weight already falls inside it and running unbounded moved the live number 257.45 → 259.61 (0.8%). The per-BAR sigma and both medians stay flat measures over that same window — only the session statistic changes. (2) THE MULTIPLE. 0.4σ was calibrated in feat-096 as 'one median 30-min bar range' at a 283-pt reference sigma; by 2026-08-11 it had drifted to ~1.5 bar ranges and to 1.43x the operator's ~102-pt average rotation — the engine was rejecting trades of exactly the size the operator normally takes. Re-tuned to 0.3σ (~77 pts at that bundle's 257-pt weighted sigma, ~85 at the 283-pt reference): ~0.75 of a rotation, 3.1x the fixed 25-pt operational stop, and still ABOVE feat-095's 0.25σ noise band, which is the one property of the old default worth keeping and the reason this is 0.3 and not lower. This is a RE-TUNE of the multiple only — feat-096's decision to store the floor in session sigma is untouched, as are the standoff (0.005σ) and chase (0.02σ) gates. Also applies the two migrations: 20260809140000_volatility_scaled_gates.sql had been committed-but-unapplied since 2026-08-09, so config still carried significant_move_pts=50 while fetchConfigRow silently padded the sigma default — the operator's /settings value was dead and only /settings surfaced the flag.
features.evidence: 2026-08-11: `lib/engine/volatilityScale.ts` gained `ewMeanSigma()` (exported, normalizes its own weights, oldest-first ordering) and `SESSION_SIGMA_DECAY = 0.75`; both estimators' `sessionSigmaPts` now route through it while `barSigmaPts`, `medianBarRangePts` and `medianSessionRangePts` keep their flat aggregation over the unchanged 10-session window. `DEFAULT_SIGNIFICANT_MOVE_SIGMA` 0.4 → 0.3 in `lib/engine/scaledGates.ts`. Verified by replaying bundle b6f71b2e through `computeEngineFacts` before and after: sessionSigmaPts 363.9 → 257.45 and the significant-move floor 145.56 → 77.24 pts, which is under the 87-pt span price sat in — so both near borders (29718.75 short / 29631.75 long) now qualify as entry anchors where before only the 246-pt and 203.5-pt outer walls did. Every pre-existing hand-computed fixture in `volatilityScale.test.ts` survived UNCHANGED because those fixtures hold their sessions identical, under which a weighted mean and a flat RMS agree by construction; five new tests cover what only appears once sessions differ (hand-computed 218.6 on a 600/400/200 contraction vs the retired RMS's 260.79; order-sensitivity on an identical multiset of sessions, which a flat RMS cannot distinguish; a 900-pt shock nine sessions old moving the scale 8.4 pts where the RMS moved it 85.8; ewMeanSigma edge cases; and the 94.4% weight-capture that justifies not widening the window). `scaledGates.test.ts` gained a regression test pinning the 2026-08-11 failure directly — the floor must clear the 87-pt span at that bundle's 257.45-pt sigma, and 0.4σ must not. features.name: Replace the ATR normalizer with the measured sigma — one volatility measure
features.description: Second half of the 2026-08-12 one-measure decision (see feat-113): the ATR NORMALIZER is replaced by feat-095's measured sigma, so the engine ships a single answer to "how big is a point right now". Today it ships two and they disagree IN THE PAYLOAD: on chart-data/htf_bar_data.rolling.csv the analyze prompt carries `htfStructure.atrPoints` 116.23 (Wilder, 14 bars, ALL bars including overnight) next to `volatilityScale.medianBarRangePts` 96.13 (RTH-only) as two answers to the same 30-min question, while `parkinson.barSigmaPts` 74.68 is computed and never shipped. They are the same quantity in different conventions — Parkinson converts a range to a sigma by dividing ~1.665, and 116.23/1.665 = 69.8 against barSigmaPts 74.68 agrees within ~7%. Changes: drop `computeAtr`, `ATR_PERIOD_BARS` and the `atrPoints` field from lib/engine/htfStructure.ts; convert `rotation.extentAtr` and `currentVsSwings.fromLastSwingHighAtr`/`fromLastSwingLowAtr` to sigma multiples through the existing `sigmaOfPoints()`; rewrite the eval prompt's HTF line (lib/eval/prompt.ts:231-254) so "30-min ATR N pts" and "an adverse move well inside 1 rotation/a few ATR is rotation noise" speak in sigma against the existing SIGMA_NOISE_MAX band; ship `parkinson.barSigmaPts` in the analyze/update volatilityScale rule so the 30-min horizon has ONE public number; update the htfStructure rules (lib/analyze/prompt.ts:331, :353 and lib/update/prompt.ts:148, :164) and the ATR references in knowledge/doctrine/chart-reading.md:14,58 and knowledge/system/output-briefing.md:12. Two consequences to DESIGN for rather than discover. (1) ORDERING — engineFacts computes htfStructure at ~line 603 and volatilityScale at ~750, so the scale must move ahead of the structure read (or the normalization move downstream of both). (2) DEGRADATION — ATR needed 14 bars and always returned a number, while computeVolatilityScale returns null under MIN_SIGMA_ESTIMATION_SESSIONS (3 complete RTH sessions), so every converted field gains a null path the prompts must degrade on ("the scale is unmeasured", the wording the volatilityScale rule already uses). This closes by construction the second finding originally filed under feat-113 — that `computeAtr` ran over the full export including overnight bars while feat-095's sigma deliberately excludes them (116.23 all-bars vs 143.10 RTH-only on the same export, a 23% gap): barSigmaPts is RTH-only by definition, so the disagreement has nowhere left to live. NOT IN SCOPE: the MGI "ATR High"/"ATR Low" chart levels — see feat-113. Verification: ./init.sh green; htfStructure.test.ts converted (its ATR normalization tests become sigma normalization, including a null-scale degradation case); tests/eval.runEval.test.ts and the prompt-data sync gate pass with no "ATR" string reachable from any engine-computed field; a repo-wide grep for computeAtr/atrPoints/extentAtr/*Atr returns only the MGI level names.

features.name: Fix double-top pivot annihilation and date the defining rotation
features.description: Live defect found 2026-08-21 in briefing edfa06a2 (bundle 8455eacd, a FRESH bundle: bars through 2026-08-21 10:00 chart time, price 29359.5). The briefing read "Range: mixed confirmed swings, so no directional integrity qualifier applies. The current 78-point rotation spans 29321.25 to 29399.25" — a rotation whose two legs confirmed at 21:30 and 23:30 the PREVIOUS day, while the live session had already traded 29220–29539. The model reported the engine fact faithfully; the fact was wrong. ROOT CAUSE: `findPivots` (lib/engine/htfStructure.ts) disqualified a candidate on a NON-STRICT comparison against BOTH windows, so two bars with an identical extreme inside the ±SWING_PIVOT_STRENGTH window annihilate each other and neither confirms. That session's high 29539.00 printed twice — 06:30 and 07:30, four bars apart, exactly at the ONH — so NO swing high from the session entered the sequence. The knock-on is what made it dangerous: with the high erased the sequence read 'mixed' → state 'range', and integrity is only computed for 'up'/'down', so feat-064's real-time squaring — the one mechanism built to stop a lagging swing read shipping unqualified — was switched OFF by the same bug that caused the staleness. Measured over the 2955-bar export: 5 tie annihilations in ~3 months, all highs — rare, but landing precisely on double-tested extremes. CHANGES. (1) Asymmetric tie rule in the shared `findPivots`: strictly above the left window, at or above the right, so the EARLIEST bar of an equal-extreme cluster is the pivot — it also confirms soonest, which matters for a read already lagging 5 bars. On the incident export this yields last swing high 29539.00 @ 2026-08-21 06:30, state 'up', rotation 217.75 pts / 3.3 ATR, integrity 'under-test' (~82% retrace) instead of 'range' + a 78-pt overnight band. (2) `lib/engine/intradayTrend.ts` kept a PRIVATE copy of the same rule running on exec bars, which tie far more often at 750-volume granularity and feed `intradayTrend.direction` (the fact that awards the primary objective); it now shares htfStructure's finder, whose bar parameter is widened to a structural `PivotBar` both bar types satisfy. `lib/engine/htfFlow.ts` already shared the finder and inherits the fix. (3) `rotation` gains `highDateTime`/`lowDateTime`: "most recent CONFIRMED" is not "current", the two legs need not come from the same session, and an undated span reads as the live range — the analyze/update/eval prompts and knowledge/doctrine/chart-reading.md + knowledge/system/output-briefing.md now forbid "the current rotation" and require the span dated whenever a leg predates the live session. Even with the tie fixed the incident's low leg is still 23:30 the prior day against a session low of 29220 — inherent fractal lag the prose must disclose, not a bug to tune away.

features.evidence: 2026-08-26 (branch feat-127-build-plan): knowledge/schema/job-plan.schema.ts (flat Zod JobPlan: meta {plannerRevision, asOf, instrument, symbol, tradingDay, bundleId, inputFingerprint, sourceHashes x7, visionPromptRevision, visionModelId} + geometryRefs {price, references, bands} + context (feat-126 JobContext) + lean + plays[] (max 4) + pruned[] + standDownReasons[] + warnings[] + status ready|insufficient; superRefine pins stance<->direction, mid-zone<->stand-down, continuation<->build-beyond, invalidation on the far side, destinations ordered in play direction, R11 deadline on hold-traverse only, armed needs a grounding, one primary at rank 1, insufficient => no plays; NO appliesWhenOpen / confidence) and lib/job-plan/{buildPlan,playCandidates,playGrammar,destinationChain,planPrecedence,planTypes,playText,runPlanner}.ts — pure, deterministic, no clock reads. Play = stance (rebid|reoffer|continuation|stand-down), direction (long|short|two-way), condition from the five-condition grammar (hold-traverse | look-and-fail | build-beyond-continuation | approach-failure | mid-zone-two-way), band (id/label/low/high/anchor/members/role/side/distance/R9 triggerStatus + PriceProvenance), trigger text, activation {state armed|conditional, grounding failed-look|approach-failure|accepted|holding-side|defense|mid-zone|none, evidence, factAt, asOf, rulesFired, demoted}, invalidation {low, high, side below|above|either, condition, thenSeek flip stage, provenance}, destinations[] = conditional stage chain (expect hold|rebid|reoffer|gate-continuation; a gate stage carries beeline {dontCounter: true, destination} together), responseDeadline (R11: 30 min AS TEXT, evaluatedByPlanner: false literal, hold-traverse only, a test greps the planner modules for the constant), dont, uncertaintyBand (box-expansion, uiOnly: true, derived-and-labeled +/- merge around a PROVISIONAL JBA edge only), summary (08-11 one-liner). Grammar: one play per candidate band grounded in its freshest origin fact (failed look -> look-and-fail; approach failure -> approach-failure fade; accepted -> continuation, fade at that band suppressed; holding side / >=2 session defenses -> hold-traverse) else the watched default (look-and-fail at JBA/overnight/prior-day edges, hold-traverse elsewhere, activation conditional); guards: holding side only within 2x merge and on the band's own side, acceptance only when the band was crossed inside the window. R12 (rules.ts r12SkipBand / r12OriginRank / r12WithinPlayCap + MAX_ARMED_BANDS_PER_SIDE 2 / MAX_PLAYS 4 / ORIGIN_PRECEDENCE): <= 2 bands per side nearest-first within reach, lone lowest-tier (mgi-other and below) skipped absolutely, plus the enclosing zone's edges within reach, bands price is inside always in; every pruned band listed with its reason. Precedence tiers: insufficient input -> no plan; EARLY failed look 0 > LATE 1 > approach failure 2 > accepted 3 > mid-zone stand-down 4 > holding side 5 > defense 6 > watched 7 > R9-demoted 8; then fresher, then enclosing edges, then weekly-value alignment (re-orders, never manufactures), then distance, then id; cap 4; lean = rank-1 play only when a fact backs it. runPlanner({ files: {jobStudyDaily, jobStudyWeekly, mgi, execBars, htfBars} raw text, profileNodes | null, asOf wall clock, meta? }) -> { plan, warnings }: parse failures THROW (JobStudyParseError / PlannerInputError mgi_too_large|mgi_invalid|exec_bars_invalid|htf_bars_invalid|input_invalid); insufficient geometry RETURNS status insufficient. features.name: Axis-free profile rendering with normalized-position reads
features.description: Operator idea: the price axis is the one thing on the profile image the vision model has to READ rather than SEE, and reading it is the error-prone step. Add an AXIS-FREE render variant that omits the axis (and every other digit) entirely; the model returns each node's normalized vertical position (0 = bottom edge, 1 = top) and CODE converts it to price from the span the image is already known to cover. A FRACTION, not a pixel row, so it survives a render-size change without invalidating the few-shot examples or the bench cache. Pixel budget is generous: on the 900x1400 render the R1 match tolerance (ES 5 / NQ 20 pts) is 31-52 px, i.e. 2-4 % vertical accuracy. Scope is a PARALLEL path, not a replacement -- the price-axis path is live in production (config.profile_vision_model_id is set) and the operator A/Bs the two arms himself. Pieces: RenderOptions.axis (default true) suppressing axis line/ticks/labels/gridlines and giving the freed 108 px gutter to the bars, with POC/VAH/VAL lines + value-area shade KEPT as the only visible calibration anchors (labels lose their price, keep their tag); profileNodesReadNormalizedSchema as the axis-free wire contract and profileNodesReadEitherSchema for a read of unknown provenance, both FLAT objects (OpenAI rejects root unions); conversion at the identifyProfileNodes CALL BOUNDARY against the TILE span so consensus, the bench scorer and the planner keep seeing prices only; an axis-free prompt mode (yLow/yHigh output rules, POC/VAH/VAL/current stated as fractions alongside their prices, an override for the two criteria that name the axis) threaded through the SAME buildVisionPrompt; normalized few-shot expectations DERIVED mechanically from the price ones; and an `axis-free` bench variant (tiles: 1 -- tiling exists because axis text shrinks, and there is no axis text). No live LLM calls.
features.evidence: 2026-08-30 (PR #178, branch feat-135-axis-free-render). Renderer: RenderOptions.axis / RenderMeta.axis (default true); axis: false drops the axis line, ticks, price labels and major gridlines, moves plotRight from width-132 to width-24 (bars 744 -> 852 px, +14.5 %), and renders marker labels as bare tags -- the SVG then holds no <text> containing a digit (asserted). tileGeometry reads meta.axis loosely so a job_plans row persisted before feat-135 still maps at the axis plot width. Schema: profileNodesReadNormalizedSchema (yLow/yHigh in [0,1], the axis-free WIRE contract) and profileNodesReadEitherSchema (all four bound fields optional, exactly-one-pair enforced); all three reads share one refineRead so the count / primary / rationale rules cannot drift. Both wire schemas stay strict -- no optional fields -- because a provider in strict structured-output mode wants every property in `required`; only the never-on-the-wire `either` schema uses optionals. Conversion in identifyProfileNodes.runCall against call.tile (the TILE span, so a tiled axis-free render converts against the right window); a read that fails superRefine is recorded as a failed sample, never converted. RawSample.read, consensus, bench, planner and the persisted shape are untouched. Prompt: VISION_PROMPT_REVISION vision-2026-08-30.7 -> vision-2026-08-30.8; ROLE_AXIS_FREE + OUTPUT_RULES_AXIS_FREE + AXIS_FREE_NOTE selected by meta.axis inside the SAME buildVisionPrompt; the axis-mode snapshot is BYTE-IDENTICAL (only insertions in prompt.test.ts.snap), so the A/B's price arm runs the live prompt unchanged. Few-shot: manifest gains expectedNormalized, generated by scripts/few-shot-normalize.ts (--check verifies) and asserted in prompt.test.ts to equal toNormalizedRead(expected, span) and to convert back to the price file's prices within span*1e-6. Bench: VARIANTS['axis-free'] = { axis: false, tiles: 1 }; makeGenerate now forwards the SCHEMA identifyProfileNodes hands it (it hardcoded profileNodesReadSchema, which would have sent the wrong contract on the axis-free arm) and the response cache validates with the either-schema, replaying an entry only when it parses under the current arm's schema. scripts/render-profile.ts gains --axis-free. Tests: 192 in lib/job-plan/profile-vision (was 151) -- round-trip price->fraction->price on four real golden profiles (2026-02-13 NQ 845 pts, 2026-02-20 ES 135 pts, 2026-03-06 NQ 898 pts, 2026-06-02 ES) within span*1e-6, which is < tolerance/1000; axis-free SVG carries no digit and rasterizes to a valid 900x1400 PNG; schema both/neither/half-pair rejected and each pair alone accepted; the boundary test proves no consumer sees a fraction. NO live LLM calls (stubbed generate throughout). Codex gate PASS first run (0 P0, 0 P1, 2 P2), both P2 fixed, none dismissed: (1) the prompt said y=0 was the IMAGE's bottom edge while the conversion maps across the PLOT area -- a literal reading biases every fraction by +-2.9 % at the extremes, ~24 pts on the widest NQ profile, MORE than the 20-pt tolerance; the text now anchors to the lowest/highest BAR and names the blank margins as outside the scale; (2) an out-of-span current price is still LABELLED at the plot edge by the renderer, so 'not in this image' contradicted the picture -- undrawn markers now say 'no line for it in this image' and the current price says where its label is pinned and that it is not a scale anchor. Round 2 raised one more P2, also fixed: the either-schema accepted a complete pair plus a stray HALF of the other pair, and an arm-specific z.object parse would strip the stray field and replay a self-contradicting cached band as clean -- resolveBand now rejects on the PRESENCE of any field of the non-selected pair.
